title: introduce-rag-microservice-tool-calling-docker-quickstart
author: Priya Kapoor
description: Add a compact, docker-first RAG microservice quickstart that demonstrates function/tool-calling, streaming responses, and a minimal KV cache for low-latency private deployments. Motivation: customers frequently ask for a small, deployable reference that shows how to wire Redwood SDK into a tiny service that handles document retrieval, model orchestration, and calls external tools (search + knowledge connector) with clear observability hooks. This PR delivers: 1) examples/rag-microservice/ - a ready-to-run template (Dockerfile + docker-compose) that boots a single-node instance with an embedded retriever, Redwood SDK integration, and a simple tool interface for invoking a mock search API. 2) README quickstart that walks through local Docker run, env var configuration for hosted vs. private endpoints, and sample curl/SDK calls for streaming. 3) src/agent.ts - an opinionated agent orchestration example that shows stepwise tool-calling (retrieve -> call tool -> synthesize -> stream) and includes backpressure-friendly streaming hooks. 4) docs/quickstarts/rag-microservice.md - a short doc page for the docs site (to be pulled into the quickstarts index) focused on deployment modes and production considerations (batching, KV cache warmup, model pinning). 5) Integration test and CI job to validate startup and a basic end-to-end conversation sample. Checklist: - [x] Minimal runnable example (Docker) - [x] Clear env var examples for redwood API key / private endpoint - [x] Streaming example with SDK snippets for JS and Python - [x] Observability pointers (which telemetry hooks to wire) - [x] Integration test in CI that runs container and POSTs a sample query Notes on differences vs existing RAG quickstarts: this template is intentionally compact and implements tool-calling as explicit function stubs (mock_search, metadata_indexer) so customers can replace with their production connectors easily. It emphasizes local Docker-first flow and opts for a lightweight on-disk document index rather than a full vector DB to keep the quickstart low-friction. Compatibility: works with Redwood SDK >= 0.9.0; recommends model variants that support streaming token-level responses. Backwards-incompatible changes: none. Related Linear tasks: ENG-4991 implement micro-quickstart; PM-221 doc alignment for quickstarts. Merge rationale: small, self-contained, high-value example for engineering onboarding and support triage.
